ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee; no refund or account action; optionally note the rider's NS-7 request for goodwill (not an entitlement) in RydeHELP.
ruling.reasoning:
The case is routed by the rider-side cancellation: cancelled_by = rider at 08:46:40, 6 min 40 s after the 08:40:00 acceptance [F4]. Under NS-0 a rider cancellation on an on-demand booking goes to NS-4, and since the cancellation came beyond the 3-minute free-cancellation window, the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable as of right [F4][F7][NS-0][NS-4].

The complaint's factual premise — "the driver had not even arrived" — is contradicted by the system records, which override statements: the platform recorded arrival at 08:41:25 [F5], the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 08:42:15 while 40 m from the pickup [F6], and he was stationary 41 m away from 08:42:00 until the 08:46:40 cancellation, with a closest approach of 39 m [F3][F1]. That is a continuous in-range wait of 4 min 25 s after the tap, exceeding the NS-1 (iii) threshold [F6][NS-1]. So even if one tested the fee on the driver-side no-show construction, NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are met and NS-2 (refund plus flag) is unavailable [F6][F5][NS-1][NS-2]. Note that even a genuine non-arrival would not be a free-cancellation ground under NS-4 [F4][NS-4]. Under the NS-1 threshold rule the trace marks the four-minute wait as settled; no evidence gap arises, so no escalation is warranted on that basis.

The rider's own chat message at 08:45 — "Sorry, plans changed, I will cancel" — reads as her own change of mind, not driver fault, and the driver's 08:42 message was a neutral position report giving notice the car was waiting [F10][F9]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped [F11], which NS-4/NS-7 do not require to be disturbed [F11][NS-4].

The charge itself is the published $6.61 with multiplier 1.0×, so there is no unpublished or overstated add-on to refund under FARE-1 [F7][F8][FARE-1]. Traffic and weather records are irrelevant here and show nothing needing exemption [F13][F14][F15].

The rider's residual ask is discretionary relief under NS-7; NS-7 makes any refund a discretionary voucher, not an entitlement, and nothing in the clauses displaces the NS-4 outcome [F16][NS-7]. Profile facts (rider one dispute, zero upheld; driver two upheld no-show disputes) cannot decide the case, and no flag arises: NS-2's flag condition is not triggered [F16][F17][NS-2][RD-6]. Safety was screened: the chat, statement and complaint contain only an arrival notice, a cancellation notice and a post-trip statement — no threat, abuse or dangerous-driving allegation [F9][F10][F12][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider asks for a goodwill voucher, but NS-7 makes a refund discretionary for Ryde and creates no entitlement; the fee is chargeable under NS-4 (cancellation 6 min 40 s after acceptance, beyond the 3-minute window) [F4][F7][F16][NS-7][NS-4].

Correct in result but for the wrong reason: no flag attaches to the rider not because of the profile history but because no NS-2 condition is breached (the driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 40 m within the 200 m radius and waited continuously >3 min) [F6][F16][NS-2][RD-6].
